pr.title: Fold arithmetic identities in GVN
pr.description:
Extracted from https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/111344

This PR implements a few arithmetic folds for unary and binary operations.
This should take care of the missed optimizations introduced by https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/116012.
pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The only defective step in this PR's "incorrect transformation" is the pre-guard `as_bits` implementation: it calls `self.ecx.read_scalar(constant)` on a constant whose layout may be a wide pointer (`Abi::ScalarPair`, e.g. `*const [u8]` or `*const dyn Trait`). In the actual interpreter that does not silently fold the fat pointer to a scalar; `read_immediate` accepts `ScalarPair`, then `Immediate::to_scalar()` hits `bug!("Got a scalar pair where a scalar was expected")`, i.e. a compiler ICE. Patch 4 ("Do not read a scalar on a non-scalar layout") adds the `layout.abi.is_scalar()` guard precisely to avoid that ICE; the added `wide_ptr_ops` test is a compile-time regression test. An ICE has no defined Miri execution and produces no runtime value, so it cannot be encoded as the required pair of Miri-passing functions with different outputs. The other edits in this PR are semantics-preserving invariants for defined inputs: `x+0`, `x-0`, `x*0`, `x*1`, `x/1`, `0/x`, `x%1`, `0%x`, bitwise neutral/absorbing/ALL_ONES, `x-x`, `x^x`, `x==x`, `x!=x`, `--x`, `!!b`, `!(a==b)`/`!(a!=b)`, and static array/unsize `Len`. Their type guards exclude floats; checked ops correctly produce `(result, false)` because the identities cannot overflow; and the divisor-zero, shift-overflow, and neg/div-overflow checks are separate MIR asserts that are not removed by folding. Constructing e.g. a "compare only the data pointer of a fat pointer" function would not model the actual historical code (which ICEs) and would be a fabricated rewrite, so no source-grounded counterexample pair can be validated.

analysis.originalLogic: GVN's `simplify_binary` only inserted a symbolic `Value::BinaryOp`/`Value::CheckedBinaryOp` after simplifying operands, so algebraic identities such as `x + 0`, `x * 0`, `x - x`, `x & ALL_ONES`, `x == x`, etc. remained in MIR. `simplify_unary` did not exist, and `Rvalue::Len` always became a symbolic `Value::Len`. The PR adds `simplify_binary`, `simplify_unary`, and `simplify_len`. From the patch: `fn simplify_binary(...)`, with `lhs_ty.is_integral() || lhs_ty.is_bool() || lhs_ty.is_char() || lhs_ty.is_any_ptr();`, and `// Floats are weird enough that none of the logic below applies.` Neutral elements include `(BinOp::Add | BinOp::BitOr | BinOp::BitXor, Ok(0), Err(p))` and `(BinOp::Mul, Ok(1), Err(p))`; absorbing elements include `(BinOp::Mul | BinOp::BitAnd, _, Ok(0))`; also `// Sub/Xor with itself.` `(BinOp::Sub | BinOp::BitXor, a, b) if a == b`. Checked folds return a tuple: `let false_val = self.insert_bool(false);` then `Some(self.insert_tuple(vec![result, false_val]))`, otherwise `Some(result)`. Unary folds include `(UnOp::Not, Value::UnaryOp(UnOp::Not, inner)) => return Some(*inner)` and the `(UnOp::Not, Value::BinaryOp(BinOp::Eq, lhs, rhs)) => {` arm returning `Value::BinaryOp(BinOp::Ne, *lhs, *rhs)`. Len folds static array length or unsize-cast metadata, else `// Fallback: a symbolic Len.`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically GVN performed no arithmetic-identity folding: it left `Add(x, 0)`, `Sub(x, 0)`, `Mul(x, 0)`, `Mul(x, 1)`, `Rem(x, 1)`, `BitAnd(x, 0)`, `BitOr(x, 0)`, `BitXor(x, x)`, `Shl(x, 0)`, `Shr(x, 0)`, `Eq(x, x)`, `Ne(x, x)`, `Neg(Neg(x))`, `Not(Not(b))`, `Not(Eq(a,b))`, and `Len(array)` as symbolic operations. The optimization rewrites those identity forms to the surviving operand, a constant (`const 0`, `const true`, `const false`, array length), or the complementary comparison. For checked ops the replacement is the aggregate `(result, false)` because the operation cannot overflow in these identity cases. A separate agent can construct pairs such as `opaque(x + 0)` vs `opaque(x)`, `opaque(x * 0)` vs `opaque(0)`, `opaque(x == x)` vs `opaque(true)`, `opaque(--x)` vs `opaque(x)`, `opaque(!(x == 15))` vs `opaque(x != 15)`, and `index([..; 4], 2)` vs the same with the length replaced by `const 4_usize`. Separately, before the layout guard, `as_bits` unconditionally ran `let scalar = self.ecx.read_scalar(constant).ok()?;` even when the constant's layout was a wide pointer (non-scalar); the corrected transformation is `if layout.abi.is_scalar() { ... } else { // `constant` is a wide pointer. Do not evaluate to bits. None }`. A separate agent can construct pairs comparing fat pointers such as `*const [u8]` / `*const dyn Trait` (where no bit-fold may occur) versus scalar operands (where bit-folding is valid).
analysis.inputDomain: MIR `Rvalue::BinaryOp`, `Rvalue::CheckedBinaryOp`, `Rvalue::UnaryOp`, and `Rvalue::Len` processed by the GVN pass. Binary/unary fold types are integral, bool, char, or raw pointers (`lhs_ty.is_integral() || lhs_ty.is_bool() || lhs_ty.is_char() || lhs_ty.is_any_ptr()`); floats are explicitly excluded. Identity folds require a known constant operand (bits from `self.evaluated[value]`) or equal VN indices for `x - x`, `x ^ x`, `x == x`, `x != x`. Checked operations carry a `(T, bool)` result whose overflow flag must be false. `Len` covers arrays, reborrowed fat pointers, and unsize casts, with a symbolic fallback. Wide-pointer inputs include `*const [u8]` and `*const dyn Send`; non-scalar layouts must not be read as scalars.
analysis.summary: Optimization PR adding GVN arithmetic/unary/Len identity folding. Old GVN left symbolic `Add(x,0)`, `Mul(x,0)`, `Sub(x,x)`, `Eq(x,x)`, `Neg(Neg(x))`, `Not(Eq(a,b))`, and `Len(array)`; new GVN replaces them with the surviving operand or a constant, and checked ops with `(result, false)`. Reusable correctness conditions: restrict to integral/bool/char/pointer types (not floats), compute all-ones via type size with a bool special case, preserve checked overflow/tuple form and division-by-zero checks, simplify both operands for side effects even when short-circuiting, and never call `read_scalar`/`to_bits` on a non-scalar (wide-pointer) layout.
analysis.trigger: GVN encounters an identity binary/unary operation, a `Len` on an array or unsized pointer, or a comparison with identical operands. Examples from the tests: `x + 0`, `x - 0`, `x - x`, `x * 0`, `x * 1`, `x / 1`, `0 / x`, `x % 1`, `0 % x`, `x & 0`, `x & u64::MAX`, `x | 0`, `x | u64::MAX`, `x ^ 0`, `x ^ x`, `x >> 0`, `x << 0`, `x == x`, `x != x`, `--x`, `!!b`, `!(x == 15)`, `!(x != 35)`, and indexing an array (compile-time `Len`). Checked variants are triggered under `#[rustc_inherit_overflow_checks]` as `CheckedAdd`/`CheckedSub`/`CheckedMul`. Wide-pointer comparison such as `a == b` on `*const dyn Send` or `*const [u8]` must not trigger bit-folding.
preconditions: GVN is running on MIR containing BinaryOp, CheckedBinaryOp, UnaryOp, or Len rvalues.
Binary/unary operand type satisfies lhs_ty.is_integral() || lhs_ty.is_bool() || lhs_ty.is_char() || lhs_ty.is_any_ptr(); floats are rejected.
At least one binary operand is a known constant, or both operands resolve to the same VN index for x-x / x^x / x==x / x!=x.
Checked arithmetic folding must produce an aggregate (result, false) to represent no overflow.
Division/remainder folds must leave the separate divisor-zero assert semantics intact (x/0 and x%0 are not folded to a value).
For bit-based folds, the constant layout must be scalar; wide pointers use the VnIndex path instead.
simplify_operand must be invoked on both operands before any short-circuit fold, for side effects.
pitfalls: Do not apply identity logic to floats: `// Floats are weird enough that none of the logic below applies.`
ALL_ONES is type-width dependent: `ones == layout.size.truncate(u128::MAX)` plus the special case `(layout.ty.is_bool() && ones == 1)`; hardcoding 0xFF or u128::MAX is wrong.
For checked ops the result is not just the value: it must be `Some(self.insert_tuple(vec![result, false_val]))` with `insert_bool(false)`, because identities never overflow.

Do not fold `x / 0` or `x % 0` into a value; the MIR still must contain the divisor-zero check. Safe Div/Rem folds are only `x / 1`, `x % 1`, `0 / x`, `0 % x` (and the 0-lhs absorbing cases for Mul/Div/Rem/BitAnd/Shl/Shr), not arbitrary rhs zero.

The absorbing rule for `Mul`/`BitAnd`/`Rem` with a zero/one constant and the neutral rules depend on which side the constant is on; both `(op, Ok(k), Err(p))` and `(op, Err(p), Ok(k))` cases are enumerated explicitly.

`x == x` / `x != x` folding is valid because the same VnIndex denotes the same value; do not generalize to proving inequality of different operands: `otherwise, do nothing, as we do not try to prove inequality.`
Calling `read_scalar`/`to_bits` on a non-scalar layout (wide pointer) is incorrect; guard with `if layout.abi.is_scalar()` and return `None` for fat pointers.
Do not skip `simplify_operand` on the second operand when the first causes an early fold: `// Only short-circuit options after we called `simplify_operand` // on both operands for side effect.`
`Len` folding must follow fat-pointer metadata through reborrows and unsize casts; a missed or wrong cast direction should fall back to symbolic `Value::Len` rather than guess.
Do not assume a retained old test name/comment means the old transformation is still expected; compare actual value assignments in the decoded diffs.
analysis.testStrategy: Add/update `tests/mir-opt/gvn.rs` functions with `// EMIT_MIR gvn.<fn>.GVN.diff` and `// CHECK:` assertions that the identity form disappears and the expected folded value/operand remains. Examples in the patch: `// CHECK: opaque::<u64>(_1)` for `x + 0`, `x - 0`, `x * 1`, `x / 1`, `x | 0`, `x & u64::MAX`, `x ^ 0`, `x >> 0`, `x << 0`; `// CHECK: opaque::<u64>(const 0_u64)` for `x - x`, `x * 0`, `x % 1`, `0 % x`, `x & 0`, `x ^ x`; `// CHECK: opaque::<bool>(const true)` / `const false` for `x == x` / `x != x`; `// CHECK: opaque::<u64>(const u64::MAX)` for `x | u64::MAX`. For checked arithmetic assert both the folded value and `// CHECK: assert(!const false,` so the no-overflow tuple flag is tested. Test unary double negation and comparison complements with `// CHECK: opaque::<i64>(_1)` and paired `// CHECK: opaque::<bool>([[c]])` lines ("Both lines should test the same thing."). Test `Len` via array indexing, including const-generic `const N`, asserting `_4 = const 4_usize` / `const 5000_usize` / `const N` and folded `assert(const true, ...)`. Add a `wide_ptr_ops` test over `*const dyn Send` and `*const [u8]` to ensure fat-pointer comparisons do not scalar-bit-fold while thin/symbolic folds remain. Run both panic-abort and panic-unwind variants. Include a float case (not covered in patch) to verify no folding occurs.
